simple_definition: A person who starts and runs their own business, taking on financial risk.
detailed_definition: A person who organizes and operates a business or businesses, taking on greater than normal financial risks to do so.
examples: Young entrepreneurs are increasingly launching startups straight out of university.
She became a successful entrepreneur after starting her own tech company.
ielts_relevance: Common in essays about business, innovation, and employment.

simple_definition: The activity of setting up and running a business.
detailed_definition: The activity of setting up a business or businesses, taking on financial risks in the hope of profit.
examples: The government launched a program to encourage entrepreneurship among young people.
Entrepreneurship requires creativity, resilience, and a willingness to take risks.
ielts_relevance: Common noun form in economy and education essays.

simple_definition: A period of temporary economic decline.
detailed_definition: A period of temporary economic decline during which trade and industrial activity are reduced.
examples: Many businesses closed during the global economic recession.
The country is showing signs of recovering from the recession.
ielts_relevance: Core economic term for Writing Task 2 essays about the economy.

simple_definition: Not significantly affected by an economic downturn.
detailed_definition: Describes an industry, job, or investment that remains stable or profitable even during an economic recession.
examples: Healthcare is often considered a recession-proof industry.
Investors look for recession-proof stocks during uncertain times.
ielts_relevance: Useful specific term for economy and career essays.

simple_definition: A general increase in prices and fall in the purchasing value of money.
detailed_definition: A sustained increase in the general price level of goods and services in an economy over a period of time.
examples: Rising inflation has made everyday goods more expensive for families.
The central bank raised interest rates to control inflation.
ielts_relevance: Essential economic vocabulary for Task 2 essays.

simple_definition: The state of being without a paid job.
detailed_definition: The state of not having a job despite being able and willing to work.
examples: Youth unemployment remains a serious challenge in many developing countries.
The government introduced new policies to reduce unemployment.
ielts_relevance: Extremely common IELTS topic in employment and economy essays.

simple_definition: All the people who work in a company, industry, or country.
detailed_definition: The people engaged in or available for work, either in a country or company or in a particular field.
examples: Automation is expected to displace a significant portion of the workforce.
Women now make up nearly half of the global workforce.
ielts_relevance: Common noun for essays about employment and the economy.

simple_definition: Payment or reward for work or services provided.
detailed_definition: Money paid for work or a service; formal term for salary or wages.
examples: The job offers competitive remuneration and excellent benefits.
Employees are demanding fairer remuneration for their overtime work.
ielts_relevance: Formal high-band synonym for 'salary' or 'pay'.

simple_definition: Something that motivates or encourages someone to do something.
detailed_definition: A thing that motivates or encourages someone to do something, often a reward or benefit.
examples: The government offers tax incentives for companies that invest in renewable energy.
Bonuses are often used as an incentive to boost employee performance.
ielts_relevance: Useful when proposing solutions in Task 2 essays.

simple_definition: The rate at which goods are produced or work is completed.
detailed_definition: The effectiveness of productive effort, especially in industry, measured in terms of output per unit of input.
examples: Remote work has been shown to increase productivity for many employees.
The company invested in new machinery to boost productivity.
ielts_relevance: Common in essays about work, technology, and the economy.

simple_definition: Achieving maximum productivity with minimum wasted effort.
detailed_definition: Performing or functioning in the best possible manner with the least waste of time and effort.
examples: The new system is far more efficient than the old paper-based one.
Public transport is often a more efficient way to travel in cities.
ielts_relevance: Extremely versatile adjective across almost all IELTS topics.

simple_definition: Income generated from business activities.
detailed_definition: Income, especially of a company or organization, generated from its normal business operations.
examples: The company's revenue grew by 20% last year.
Tourism generates significant revenue for the local economy.
ielts_relevance: Common in Task 1 business/economy data descriptions.

simple_definition: The action of spending money; the amount spent.
detailed_definition: The action of spending funds, or the total amount of money spent on something.
examples: Government expenditure on healthcare has increased significantly.
Household expenditure on food rose due to inflation.
ielts_relevance: Common in Task 1 essays describing spending data.

simple_definition: To support financially, especially to help keep prices low.
detailed_definition: To support an organization or activity financially, typically to keep the price of a product or service low.
examples: The government subsidizes public transport to encourage its use.
Farmers receive subsidized loans to help them purchase equipment.
ielts_relevance: Useful verb for essays about government spending and support.

simple_definition: The transfer of a business or industry from public to private ownership.
detailed_definition: The transfer of a business, industry, or service from public to private ownership and control.
examples: The privatization of the railway system led to mixed results.
Critics argue that privatization of healthcare can increase inequality.
ielts_relevance: Common in essays comparing public and private ownership.

simple_definition: Complete control of trade in a particular good or service by one company.
detailed_definition: The exclusive possession or control of the supply of or trade in a commodity or service.
examples: The company held a virtual monopoly on the country's telecommunications industry.
Regulators are concerned about tech giants forming monopolies.
ielts_relevance: Useful for essays about business competition and regulation.

simple_definition: A large company formed by combining several smaller companies.
detailed_definition: A large corporation formed by the combination of several smaller companies, often operating in different industries.
examples: The media conglomerate owns several television networks and newspapers.
Small businesses often struggle to compete with large conglomerates.
ielts_relevance: Advanced noun for essays about big business and globalization.

simple_definition: A newly established business, typically small and innovative.
detailed_definition: A newly established company, typically small and often innovative, in its early stages of development.
examples: Many tech startups fail within their first two years.
She left her corporate job to launch her own startup.
ielts_relevance: Common modern term for business and technology essays.

simple_definition: Money invested in new businesses that have high growth potential but also high risk.
detailed_definition: Funding provided by investors to startup companies and small businesses believed to have long-term growth potential.
examples: The startup secured a large round of venture capital funding.
Venture capital firms often invest in technology and biotech companies.
ielts_relevance: Useful for advanced business and finance discussions.

simple_definition: A person or group with an interest in a business or project.
detailed_definition: A person, group, or organization that has an interest or concern in a business, project, or system.
examples: The company consulted all stakeholders before making the decision.
Employees, customers, and shareholders are all key stakeholders in a business.
ielts_relevance: Formal business term useful for high-band essays.

simple_definition: To discuss something with someone to reach an agreement.
detailed_definition: To try to reach an agreement or compromise by means of formal discussion.
examples: The two companies negotiated a new trade deal.
She successfully negotiated a higher salary during her interview.
ielts_relevance: Common verb for business and diplomacy essays.

simple_definition: The combining of two companies into one.
detailed_definition: An act or instance of combining two or more organizations, especially companies, into one.
examples: The merger between the two banks created the country's largest financial institution.
Regulators must approve any major corporate merger.
ielts_relevance: Useful business vocabulary for high-band essays.

simple_definition: To make a company smaller by reducing staff.
detailed_definition: To reduce the size of a company or organization, especially by cutting staff numbers.
examples: The company was forced to downsize after losing several major clients.
Many employees lost their jobs when the firm decided to downsize.
ielts_relevance: Common verb in essays about the economy and job losses.

simple_definition: Producing a lot of profit.
detailed_definition: Producing a great deal of profit; very profitable financially.
examples: Tourism has become a lucrative industry for the coastal town.
She turned down a lucrative job offer to pursue her passion instead.
ielts_relevance: Useful high-band adjective for describing profitable careers or industries.

simple_definition: Very careful and precise about details.
detailed_definition: Showing great attention to detail and accuracy in the way something is done.
examples: She is meticulous about checking every detail of her reports before submitting them.
The scientist kept meticulous records of every experiment.
ielts_relevance: Useful for describing careful work in a professional context.

simple_definition: Showing care and effort in one's work or duties.
detailed_definition: Having or showing care and conscientiousness in one's work or duties; persistent and hardworking.
examples: He was praised by his manager for being a diligent and reliable employee.
Diligent students tend to perform better academically.
ielts_relevance: Useful positive adjective for describing work ethic in Speaking.

simple_definition: Able to adapt or be used for many different purposes or skills.
urdu_meaning: ہمہ جہت، متنوع صلاحیتوں کا حامل
detailed_definition: Able to adapt or be adapted to many different functions or activities.
examples: Employers increasingly look for versatile employees who can handle multiple roles.
The tool is incredibly versatile and can be used for a wide range of tasks.
ielts_relevance: Common positive adjective for describing skills and abilities.

simple_definition: To work jointly with others on an activity or project.
detailed_definition: To work jointly on an activity or project with one or more other people or organizations.
examples: The two universities collaborated on a major research project.
Employees are encouraged to collaborate across different departments.
ielts_relevance: Common in essays and Speaking about teamwork and workplace culture.

simple_definition: To give a task or responsibility to someone else.
detailed_definition: To entrust a task or responsibility to another person, typically one who is less senior.
examples: Effective managers know how to delegate tasks to their team.
She struggled to delegate responsibilities, preferring to do everything herself.
ielts_relevance: Useful management vocabulary for work-related essays.

simple_definition: To observe and direct the work of others.
detailed_definition: To observe and direct the execution of a task, project, or activity.
examples: She supervises a team of twenty employees at the factory.
Teachers must supervise students closely during science experiments.
ielts_relevance: Common verb in work and management contexts.

simple_definition: Advancement to a higher position or rank.
detailed_definition: The action of raising someone to a higher position or rank, especially within a job.
examples: After five years of hard work, she finally received a promotion.
Promotions are usually based on performance and experience.
ielts_relevance: Common in Speaking Part 1/2 about career and work.

simple_definition: The feeling of contentment one gets from doing their job.
detailed_definition: A sense of fulfillment and contentment derived from performing one's job well.
examples: Job satisfaction is often more important to employees than salary alone.
Studies show a strong link between job satisfaction and productivity.
ielts_relevance: Common topic for work-life balance essays.

simple_definition: A comfortable state of equilibrium between work and personal life.
urdu_meaning: کام اور ذاتی زندگی میں توازن
detailed_definition: The balance an individual maintains between the demands of their career and the elements of their personal life.
examples: Many employees value work-life balance more than a higher salary.
Remote work has made it easier for some people to achieve work-life balance.
ielts_relevance: Very common phrase in employment and lifestyle essays.

simple_definition: Time worked beyond one's normal working hours.
detailed_definition: Time spent working beyond one's scheduled working hours, often compensated at a higher rate.
examples: She often works overtime to meet tight deadlines.
Employees are paid extra for any overtime they complete.
ielts_relevance: Common in Speaking Part 1 questions about work.

simple_definition: A period of work experience offered by an organization, often for students.
detailed_definition: A period of work experience offered by an organization for a limited period, often undertaken by students or graduates.
examples: She completed a summer internship at a major law firm.
Internships provide valuable hands-on experience for new graduates.
ielts_relevance: Common in education and career-related Speaking answers.

simple_definition: A skill or achievement that makes someone suitable for a job or task.
detailed_definition: A pass of an examination or an official completion of a course, especially one conferring status as a recognized practitioner of a profession.
examples: A university degree is a common qualification required for entry-level jobs.
She has all the necessary qualifications for the position.
ielts_relevance: Common in essays and Speaking about education and careers.

simple_definition: A document summarizing a person's education and work experience.
detailed_definition: A brief written account of personal, educational, and professional qualifications and experience, submitted with a job application.
examples: Make sure to tailor your resume to each job you apply for.
Her resume highlighted her extensive experience in marketing.
ielts_relevance: Common practical vocabulary for career-related Speaking topics.

simple_definition: To identify and recruit skilled people for a specific job.
urdu_meaning: باصلاحیت افراد کو بھرتی کے لیے تلاش کرنا
detailed_definition: To seek out and recruit a person for a senior position in a company, often approaching someone already employed elsewhere.
examples: She was headhunted by a rival firm after her success at the startup.
Companies often headhunt talented executives from their competitors.
ielts_relevance: Specific business term useful for advanced discussions about recruitment.

simple_definition: To move staff or resources to a different task or place.
detailed_definition: To move personnel or resources to a different place or task, often within the same organization.
examples: Rather than laying off staff, the company chose to redeploy them to other departments.
Resources were redeployed to the areas most affected by the disaster.
ielts_relevance: Useful for essays discussing alternatives to layoffs.

simple_definition: Very different from each other; not able to be compared.
detailed_definition: Essentially different in kind; not able to be compared or grouped together easily.
examples: The report combined data from disparate sources.
Team members came from disparate backgrounds, bringing diverse perspectives.
ielts_relevance: Advanced C2 adjective for describing diversity or contrast.

simple_definition: Dealing with problems in a practical, sensible way.
detailed_definition: Dealing with things sensibly and realistically in a way based on practical considerations rather than theory.
examples: The government took a pragmatic approach to solving the housing crisis.
She is known for being pragmatic rather than idealistic in her decision-making.
ielts_relevance: High-band adjective useful in Task 2 evaluation paragraphs.

simple_definition: Having more than one possible meaning; unclear.
detailed_definition: Open to more than one interpretation; not having one obvious meaning.
examples: The contract's wording was ambiguous and led to a legal dispute.
Her response to the question was deliberately ambiguous.
ielts_relevance: Useful adjective for critiquing unclear policies or statements.

simple_definition: Complete and including everything necessary.
detailed_definition: Complete and including everything that is necessary; thorough and full in scope.
examples: The report provides a comprehensive analysis of the country's economic situation.
Students receive a comprehensive education covering a wide range of subjects.
ielts_relevance: Common formal adjective across nearly all essay topics.

simple_definition: Relevant or applicable to a particular matter.
detailed_definition: Relevant or applicable to a particular matter; apt in the circumstances.
examples: She asked several pertinent questions during the interview.
The report includes all the pertinent facts about the case.
ielts_relevance: Sophisticated adjective useful in academic Writing Task 2.

simple_definition: Of considerable importance, size, or worth.
detailed_definition: Of considerable importance, size, or worth; large in amount or degree.
examples: The company reported a substantial increase in profits this year.
A substantial number of people opposed the new policy.
ielts_relevance: One of the most useful quantifying adjectives for Task 1 and Task 2.

simple_definition: So small or unimportant as to be not worth considering.
detailed_definition: So small or unimportant as to not be worth taking into consideration; insignificant.
examples: The difference in test scores between the two groups was negligible.
The effect of the new policy on unemployment was negligible.
ielts_relevance: Opposite of 'substantial' — essential for describing small changes in Task 1.
